question: Should ClawHub preserve the current TypeScript 6/7 side-by-side compatibility setup, or sponsor a broader migration that makes TypeScript 7 the default compiler?
rationale: The current manifest matches Microsoft's recommended transition arrangement, and the proposed direct replacement fails required gates; choosing when to abandon the TypeScript 6 compatibility API is a tooling ownership decision rather than a safe mechanical repair.

options.title: Preserve the dual compiler setup
options.body: Keep TypeScript 6 as the ordinary tooling dependency, retain TypeScript 7 under `@typescript/native`, and close or supersede this direct replacement PR.

options.title: Sponsor a full TypeScript 7 migration
options.body: Update incompatible tools, configuration, and scripts in a focused migration and require all static, unit, package, type/build, HTTP, and browser gates to pass.

recommendation.title: Preserve the dual compiler setup
recommendation.body: Keep TypeScript 6 as the ordinary tooling dependency, retain TypeScript 7 under `@typescript/native`, and close or supersede this direct replacement PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The same compatibility arrangement is used in adjacent OpenClaw tooling, making steipete the best available routing candidate despite incomplete target-repository blame data.
